frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Fore-position on an ordered axis: being, coming, or placing at the front/ahead, prior to what follows — covering spatial leading-position and temporal anteriority as one axis, systematically opposed to '-x-r (behind/later).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Fore-position on an ordered axis: being, coming, or placing at the front/ahead, prior to what follows — covering spatial leading-position and temporal anteriority as one axis, systematically opposed to '-x-r (behind/later).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 48 occurrences the root marks "the ahead-slot." Form II qaddama (27x) = cause something to occupy the slot ahead of you: deeds sent forward to meet you at reckoning (bimA qad~amat >aydiyhim, mA qad~amat li-gad 59:18), a charity presented in advance (58:12-13), nothing put forward ahead of God and His Messenger (49:1), a warning sent ahead (50:28). Form V (48:2, 74:37) = move oneself into the ahead-slot vs. lag. Form X (10:49, 16:61, 34:30, 7:34, participle 15:24) = seek to be ahead of an appointed point vs. seek delay. Form I: Pharaoh at the front leading his people (11:98); God advancing upon their deeds (25:23). The noun qadam/aqdAm names the fore-stepping limb — one's advanced stance — hence "make firm our feet" in confrontation (2:250, 3:147, 47:7, 8:11), a foot slipping after firmness (16:94), and qadam Sidq, a footing of truth deposited ahead with their Lord (10:2). aqdamUn (26:76) = the more-prior forefathers; qadIm (12:95, 36:39, 46:11) = long-prior, standing since before.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue = fore-position/anteriority. FORM II adds causative transfer (make X be ahead of oneself), and in 21 of 27 cases the eschatological "deeds meeting you later" sense comes from CONTEXT (reckoning scenes, li-gad, ind Allah) plus the reflexive li-anfusikum construction, not from the root. Form V adds self-positioning; Form X adds conative "seek/attempt the ahead-slot"; the paired antonym constructions with '-x-r (9 occurrences) belong to construction, not root. Noun qadam is a LEXICALIZATION: the limb of forward stepping/standing; firmness-of-feet and slipping-of-foot readings are context (battle steadfastness, oath-breaking). qadIm/aqdam add only adjectival quality and elative morphology over temporal priority.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 41:29 ("najAalhumA taHta aqdAminA" — beneath our feet) and 55:41 (seized by forelocks and feet): here feet are mere body parts, even the lowest point, so the fore-position residue is carried only by the lexicalized noun (the forward-stepping limb) rather than demonstrated by context. Secondary strain: 25:23 "qadimnA ilA mA amilU," where Form I reads as arrival/advancing-upon; presence requires reading it as coming into the position before/at their deeds.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: A narrower hypothesis — "sending deeds ahead for future reckoning" — fits the dominant Form II cluster but fails 11:98 (spatial leading), the foot nouns, and qadIm/aqdamUn; it is a Form II + context effect, not the root. A purely temporal hypothesis ("oldness/priority in time") fails 11:98 and the battle-feet cluster. Both collapse into the broader fore-position axis, which survives all 48.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from s-b-q, which internally denotes competitive outstripping — getting ahead OF someone/something in relative motion (46:11 even contains both: "mA sabaqUnA ilayhi ... ifk qadIm") — whereas q-d-m denotes occupying the fore-slot on an axis without implying a race. Distinct from the bayna yaday construction (mere spatial frontness as location), with which qaddama combines rather than overlaps (49:1, 58:12). Its unique signature is the systematic antonym pairing with '-x-r across Forms II, V, and X (9 occurrences), showing a stable fore/aft axis no neighboring root shares. Falsifiable: an occurrence where qdm marked posteriority, lagging, or position behind would break it; none exists in the set.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 48 confirmed occurrences reconcile with a single residue — fore-position/anteriority on an ordered axis — after subtracting form (II causative, V reflexive, X conative), construction (antonym pairing with '-x-r, li-anfusikum reflexives), lexicalization (qadam = forward-stepping limb), and context (eschatological reckoning, battle steadfastness). The internal antonym system with '-x-r across three verb forms gives unusually strong axis evidence, and the qadam Sidq occurrence (10:2) bridges the foot cluster and the sending-ahead cluster. Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG because two occurrences (41:29, 55:41) exhibit the residue only through the noun's naming layer, not through context-independent demonstration, and 25:23 requires the arrival-as-advancing-upon reading; none of these contradicts the residue, but they rest on the lexicalization step rather than direct contextual confirmation.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Full coverage checked: all 48 occurrences accounted for. The proposed 'fore-position on an ordered axis, opposed to -x-r' contribution is demonstrably present across the precedence/anteriority core: V(II) qaddama (27x, 'send/put ahead'), V(V) taqaddama (48:2, 74:37 — explicitly paired with ta'akhkhara), V(X) yastaqdimun (7:34/10:49/16:61/34:30, all paired with yasta'khirun), N(X) al-mustaqdimin (15:24 vs al-musta'khirin), ADJ qadim 'old/prior' (12:95, 36:39, 46:11), N al-aqdamun 'forefathers' (26:76), V yaqdumu 'leads/goes before' (11:98). Weak-but-admissible: qadimna 'come/advance toward' (25:23, definition includes 'coming'); qadama sidq 'foremost standing/precedence' (10:2).

DECISIVE FAILURE CLUSTER: the 7 concrete qadam/aqdam ('foot/feet') occurrences — 16:94 (a foot slips), 2:250 & 3:147 & 47:7 & 8:11 (make/steady feet firm), 55:41 (forelocks and feet), 41:29 ('under our feet'). In these, the in-context meaning is the physical body part; the 'being/coming/placing at the front/ahead, prior to what follows' contribution is NOT recoverable from the verse — assigning it requires the etymological bridge (foot = advancing member), which is lexicon/memory reasoning barred as evidence. 41:29 actively inverts the axis (feet = lowest/under). Under non-negotiable root unity, one unreconciled occurrence already blocks SUPPORTED; here a coherent 7-occurrence nominal cluster resists. Hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, not SUPPORTED and not REFUTED (the precedence axis genuinely holds for ~40 occurrences).

Distinctiveness OK: residue (static fore-position/anteriority) is distinguishable from sbq (dynamic overtaking/racing — cf. 46:11 sabaquna alongside qadim) and '-w-l (first/origin), and is anchored by the recurring explicit -x-r opposition. Falsifiable: yes — the foot occurrences are the concrete falsifiers.

occurrence_dispositions.note: qadam Sidq read as a prior/precedent standing 'deposited ahead' with their Lord; precedence = anteriority, so the fore-position axis is present via the priority reading.

Singular qadam here is the established forward FOOTING. The verse's own antithesis carries the axis: thubut (firm establishment ahead, in the path of God) vs zilla/zalal (the foot slipping back). This mirrors qadam Sidq at 10:2 (a footing deposited ahead with the Lord). Root contributes the advanced-footing limb; the 'slip after firmness' is construction. Frozen fore-position axis holds cleanly.

thabbit aqdAmanA before Goliath's host = fix our feet in their forward stance, i.e. hold the advanced line and not retreat (the '-x-r / rear pole). Root supplies the fore-stepping limb / advanced stance; imperative thabbit + battle context fix it forward. Explicitly anticipated by the frozen plain-explanation. Holds.
Referenced token is al-qadim (old/long-standing date-stalk); the qaddarnahu earlier in the verse is q-d-r, not this token. Temporal anteriority present.

Identical idiom to 2:250 in the Uhud confrontation: thabbit aqdAmanA = keep our feet in the forward/holding stance against the enemy rather than being driven back. Same fore-position axis, root-level contribution intact. Holds.

Hardest case: taHta aqdAminA ... al-asfalIn foregrounds a VERTICAL/rank figure (beneath / lowest), not the fore/aft axis, and the frozen plain-explanation did not list it. But separating construction from root contribution: the vertical sense is carried by taHta and asfalIn, while the root's sole contribution to aqdAm is the noun 'feet' = the forward/advancing member of the body (qadam, opposed to the heel). That lexical fore-position motivation is intact; the trampling deployment is contextual, not a rival root sense. It genuinely holds at the level of the root's contribution, so CONSISTENT rather than forced — the axis-shift is constructional, not lexical.

yuthabbit aqdAmakum, conditioned on aiding God = divine firming of the fighters' forward footing in engagement. The feet = advanced stance held in confrontation; firmness vs being pushed to the rear is the qdm/'-x-r axis. Root contribution holds; only the participant (God as agent of thabbit) differs. Consistent.

verse_text prepends the basmala, but the token index (word 5) counts from the ayah proper and lands unambiguously on tuqaddimu ('do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger') = clear fore-position. Basmala is display-only and does not obstruct judgment.

al-nawASI wa-l-aqdAm: the mujrimUn seized by forelocks and feet — purely anatomical, with no fore/aft rhetorical play, which is why coverage flagged it. Yet the root's contribution to aqdAm is precisely 'feet = the forward member of the body' (qadam vs the rear heel/'aqib), the same qdm/'-x-r opposition instantiated anatomically. No homonymy, no competing sense; the fore-position motivation of the noun holds. CONSISTENT, not forced.
Token at word 62 is tuqaddimu (Form II, 'what you send ahead of good for yourselves'), parallel to 2:110; the earlier yuqaddiru in the verse is q-d-r, not this token.

Badr: rain sent down li-yuthabbita bihi al-aqdAm = to firm the feet (footing/ground) for the stand and advance. Same 'firm forward footing in confrontation' figure as 2:250/3:147/47:7, explicitly cited by the frozen gloss. Root supplies the fore-stance limb; context adds the firming means. Holds.
